newsitem.title: NORWAY: FIBA denies wrongdoing in MGAM-linked trade.
newsitem.headline: FIBA denies wrongdoing in MGAM-linked trade.

text.p: Norwegian holding company FIBA ASA said on Thursday its brokerage house subsidiary was not guilty of any wrongdoing in transactions linked to Morgan Grenfell Asset Management Ltd (MGAM).
A FIBA statement to the Oslo Bourse said FIBA Nordic Securities AS had examined its role in transactions involving London-based FIBA Nordic Securities (UK) Ltd (FNS) and MGAM.
"The examination has not uncovered any circumstances at FIBA Nordic Securities AS that could be subject to criticism," the statement said.
FIBA's wholly-owned subsidiary FIBA Nordic Securities AS holds a 10 percent stake in FIBA Nordic Securities (UK) Ltd, also known as FIBA Nordic Securities (FNS).

There was no immediate comment from the Norwegian Banking, Securities and Insurance Commission, which last Friday said it had launched an investigation into FIBA Nordic Securities AS and its cooperation with FNS in London. FNS is involved in the storm over holdings of three Morgan Grenfell European funds.
Morgan Grenfell Asset Management is a subsidiary of German banking giant Deutsche Bank.
FIBA said FNS had hired a lawyer to "clarify all circumstances related to its role in connection with Morgan Grenfell's transactions".
The London-based broker has denied involvement in alleged irregularities in the business of the three investment funds.
